title: Dialogue Conductor — proto scratchpad
content:
TL;DR: Sketching a lightweight orchestration layer ('Dialogue Conductor') that composes multiple small dialogue modules (micro-skills) per request. Goal: let apps mix high-fidelity LLM responses, low-cost templated replies, and deterministic tool calls in a single turn with clear cost/latency tradeoffs and developer primitives for fallbacks and persona switching. This is a personal brain-dump — rough PRD outline + user stories + quick experiment plan.

Context / motivation:
- Product teams want composite assistant behavior without stitching multiple endpoint calls in client code (costly, brittle).
- We have good building blocks (streaming, function-calls, model catalog, routing), but no simple abstraction for combining them into one coherent turn.
- Common use cases: short factual answers with a quick tool lookup; multi-part answers where the first paragraph is high-fidelity and the rest is compressed; persona-aware greetings followed by a deterministic checklist.

Core idea:
- Dialogue Conductor = orchestration policy + module registry. A request provides: (1) ordered module graph (or simple list) with execution hints, (2) per-module fidelity/cost SLA (e.g., high/medium/low), (3) persona overrides and tone profile, (4) fallbacks and time/byte budgets. The conductor executes modules, composes their outputs, applies post-processing (dedup, stitching, shortform expansion), and returns a single coherent response stream.

Key primitives (rough):
- Module types: LLM-call(module-config), Tool-call(spec), Template(snippet-id), Embed-rank(query, corpus-id), Cache-lookup(key).
- Module hints: max-tokens, latency-slo-ms, model-preference, quantization-allowed, streamable(true/false).
- Composition operators: concat, merge-best, pick-first-success, summarise(onto-length=N)
- Fallback rules: on-timeout -> next-module, on-low-confidence -> degrade-to-template, on-rate-limit -> reroute-to-dedicated.
- Persona layer: persona_id + injection points (prelude, inline, postscript) with guardrails for PII.

User stories (priority order):
1) As a product engineer, I want a single API call that tries a cheap template first and if insufficient, upgrades to a small LLM, so my UI stays snappy and I control cost. Acceptance: one request, two modules (Template then LLM), final response either template or LLM output; telemetry shows cost savings on sample traffic.
2) As an AI assistant developer, I want to run a tool-call (e.g., calendar lookup) and then have the LLM craft a response using tool output while streaming to the client, preserving low tail latency. Acceptance: tool call executes within conductor, streaming begins with a placeholder then fills; fallback policy if tool fails.
3) As a platform engineer, I want the conductor to automatically switch to a fallback model variant when a chosen model is out of capacity, with predictable latency and cost signals. Acceptance: routing policy triggers an alternative model and logs rollback reason.
4) As an enterprise customer, I want persona and branding controlled at the conductor layer so different product lines can reuse the same skill graph with different voice. Acceptance: persona injection works and respects allowed vocabulary lists.

Architectural sketch (very rough):
- Frontend (API): /v1/conductor/respond payload includes modules[], persona, budgets, route-hints.
- Conductor service: validates graph, plans parallel vs sequential execution, executes modules with adapters (ModelAdapter, ToolAdapter, TemplateAdapter), composes outputs, applies filters, returns streaming response.
- Adapters reuse existing runtime paths; conductor is mostly orchestration + lightweight composition.
- Observability: per-module token/cost/latency breakdown, composite SLI (end-to-end P95), module-level failure reasons.

Metrics to watch (success criteria):
- P95 end-to-end latency for common two-module flows < 700ms for 70% of traffic.
- Median cost per composite response reduced by >=20% vs naive full-LLM baseline for templated-heavy flows.
- Error/fallback rate <5% after first 5k requests in experiment.
- Developer friction metric: time-to-prototype (target < 2 days for an internal team).

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase A (internal): simple Template->SmallLLM flow, no streaming; run behind feature flag for internal web app. 2 weeks.
- Phase B: add Tool-call + streaming placeholders; test with calendar+faq tool combo. 3 weeks.
- Phase C: expose routing hints + persona injection beta to 2 external partners. 4 weeks.

Risks and open questions (notes to self):
- Composition semantics are tricky: how do we present confidence when parts are mixed? Need unified rationale field per module.
- Streaming + tool latency: clients may show partial text then jump. UX patterns to avoid jarring updates? incremental refinement vs replace.
- Billing model: count per-module tokens? We need a clear unit for user-facing cost estimates.
- Security: ensure tool outputs are sanitized before LLM sees them; tool calls might expose secrets.
- Cache/consistency: if the conductor caches module outputs, how to invalidate when tool state changes?

Implementation TODOs (short):
- [ ] Proto API shape (payload + examples)
- [ ] Small in-process conductor that reuses existing ModelAdapter for PoC
- [ ] Instrumentation hooks (per-module metrics) and sample dashboard
- [ ] UX playbook for streaming placeholders vs progressive append
- [ ] Draft short explainer for partners (one-pager)

Notes / loose thoughts:
- Could be a low-code UX: a 'skill builder' visual editor that drops modules and links them. Might be a follow-on.
- Consider a 'budget-first' mode where modules are chosen automatically to meet target cost/latency. That could live in Optimize.
- Use-case: customer support canned answers that add a personalized opening line via LLM; conductor composes template (answer) + LLM (opening) without two client calls.

Quick sample payload (rough, not final):
{
  "persona": "friendly_brand_x",
  "modules": [
    {"type": "template", "id": "kb-article-472", "max_tokens": 120},
    {"type": "llm", "model": "small-accelerated", "max_tokens": 64, "fallback": "tiny"}
  ],
  "composition": "merge-best",
  "budgets": {"latency_ms": 800, "cost_units": 1.2}
}

Immediate next steps: share with Maya/Noah for quick sanity check, sketch a tiny PoC in the runtime repo that wires template+llm and reports module metrics. Keep this doc as working notes.

Unresolved questions to bring up in sync:
- Maya: UX for progressive updates — do we prefer placeholder + patch or incremental append?
- SRE: how many concurrent modules should we allow per request before queueing?
- Billing: finance input on how to surface composed costs to customers.

End of scratchpad. This is intentionally fuzzy. Will iterate into a cleaner PRD once PoC shows signal.
